results.title: Figma Specs: How to Give AI Coding Agents Better Context
results.content:
Figma describes Specs as a multiplayer container for Markdown that lives on the canvas. It is rolling out in open beta to paid plans on web, desktop, and mobile, and access is expanding gradually. Specs can embed FigJam files, frames, and code layers. Users can drag in existing .md files, duplicate a Spec for parallel work, and pull data through connectors such as GitHub. When a Spec is final, the team can hand it to a coding agent through the MCP server.

A screenshot shows how an interface looks. A Spec explains why it looks that way, how it behaves, and which frames and tokens govern each decision. For a simple button, the difference may be small. For a checkout flow or a permissions-based dashboard, it determines whether the agent builds the right thing. [...] Start with one interface. Write a focused Spec, connect a compatible agent, implement in small steps, and validate the result against the original design. Then update the Spec with what you learned.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Figma Specs?

Figma Specs is a Markdown container on the Figma canvas for requirements, design rules, and technical context. It can embed frames, FigJam files, and code layers, so written instructions stay linked to the design. It is in open beta for paid plans.

### How does Figma Specs work with AI coding agents?

A compatible coding agent connects to Figma through the MCP server and reads a Spec along with the frames it links to. The Spec supplies intent and rules, and the agent uses them to plan and write code. Human review is still required. [...] ## Quick Summary: What Figma Specs Changes for AI Coding

Figma Specs is a Markdown-based container on the Figma canvas. Teams use it to write requirements, design rules, and technical notes that people and connected AI agents can both read. The Figma MCP server lets compatible coding agents read a Spec along with the material it links to.

# Figma Specs

Build with shared context across Figma, teams, and agents.

Get startedContact sales

## A container for context that can move into, out of, and across Figma.

Bring written intent, visual exploration, and technical details together for your team and your agents.

 Pull in your existing context, data, and codebase—no matter where it lives.

## Easily move between planning, designing, and coding.

Drop in data, connect external agents, and tag in teammates to help you build out your spec.

 

  ### Use Specs on the canvas or on its own

  Write out your spec where you design, or work in a separate space and drop it in when you’re ready. [...] ### Context that flows in both directions

  Pull in diagrams, tables, and designs from Figma. Or, bring in data and content from other tools via the Figma agent.

## Build with your favorite agent.

Specs gives agents structured Markdown to guide them from prototype to production.

 Tap the Figma agent to build with code layers on the canvas or ship to an external tool via MCP.
